author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correcting a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected: the booking form reopens prefilled with the visit's current date and description, an accepted correction updates that visit in place and returns the reader to the owner's record, and a refused one redisplays the form.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the reader is returned to the owner's record.
Given an accepted correction, when the owner's record is shown, then the pet holds the same number of visits as before the correction.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a refused correction, when the form is shown again, then the stored visit still holds its previous date and description.
Edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not exist, or one that belongs to another pet, is refused rather than opening or changing an unrelated record.
Edge case 4: a visit whose date has already passed is still held to the future-date rule; a correction that keeps the passed date is refused.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit — NG-5 keeps this out of scope
Deleting any record — NG-4 is untouched
A link to the correction form from the owner's record page or any other page; the owner deferred a visible entry point to a follow-up request
A distinct confirmation message for a correction; recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md
notes: No prd-autofix records since the last prd-entry; the autofix audit found nothing to judge. NG-5 is narrowed in docs/prd.md and recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-correction.md. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside the product expert's write scope and still has to be added. Four open questions the request left unanswered are recorded in docs/prd.md § Open Questions: the missing entry point, the confirmation wording (a new message needs every supported language, REQ-LANG-002), whether a passed-date visit is correctable in practice, and whether the visit under correction appears among the earlier visits listed on the form. Each was resolved by the narrowest reading of the request, not by a product answer.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction is the existing edit shape applied to a third record, not new ground. PetController already demonstrates every piece: an optional path variable on the @ModelAttribute loader (findPet, PetController.java:75-87), a paired GET/POST /edit mapping, and an in-place update of the entity already inside the aggregate (updatePetDetails, PetController.java:186-200). The write path stays OwnerRepository.save(owner) with cascade from Pet.visits, per system-design.md#persistence. No new package, type, layer, dependency, or persistence pattern. The one adjustment is to VisitController.loadPetWithVisit, which today unconditionally constructs a Visit and calls pet.addVisit; it must branch on an optional visitId. docs/system-design.md gained the REQ wiring on five Contracts rows and one state paragraph under Persistence recording the binding shape.
integration_points: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit takes @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId. Null keeps today's behaviour (new Visit, pet.addVisit). Non-null returns the visit already on the pet and adds nothing. Spring resolves the optional path variable per request, so the /visits/new mappings are unaffected — this is exactly PetController.findPet's shape.

Add Pet.getVisit(Integer id) returning the visit with that id or null, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) (Owner.java:117-127). Identity lookup inside the aggregate belongs on the entity, not in a controller stream.

GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit returns "pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm" and nothing else, mirroring PetController.initUpdateForm. Prefill is automatic: the model attribute IS the stored visit.

POST on the same path binds onto that same instance, applies the same non-future-date check, and on success calls this.owners.save(owner) with no add* call at all. Return "redirect:/owners/{ownerId}"; the template expands ownerId from the current request.

Template needs no change. The form carries no action attribute, so it posts to the current URL; the heading drops "New" because visit.isNew() is false; the previous-visits table's th:each shadows the model attribute, so it lists every persisted visit.

patterns.description: findPet — @ModelAttribute loader keyed on an optional path variable, serving both the create and the edit mapping from one controller. Copy this shape into loadPetWithVisit.

updatePetDetails — in-place update of the stored entity. Copy the intent, NOT the field-by-field copy: PetController must copy because its owner and pet model attributes come from two separate findById calls, so the bound pet is not the instance inside owner's graph. VisitController resolves owner, pet, and visit from ONE findById call, so the bound visit already is that instance and binding alone completes the update.
Owner.getPet(Integer) — identity lookup over an aggregate collection, null when absent. Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors it.
The non-future-date rule. Extract it into one private helper called by both POST handlers rather than duplicating the expression — see the note on the Web-controller deviation.

risks.risk: A second Visit record. Pet.visits is a LinkedHashSet and BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, so a freshly constructed Visit carrying the same id is a SECOND set element, and cascade ALL then writes a second row. This is the failure the acceptance criterion 'the pet holds the same number of visits' guards.
risks.mitigation: Never construct a Visit on the correction path and never call pet.addVisit or owner.addVisit there. Resolve the stored instance in loadPetWithVisit and let binding mutate it.

risks.risk: Edge case 3 (unknown visit, or a visit belonging to another pet) reached by an unscoped lookup. There is no VisitRepository, so the only route to a visit is owner -> pet -> visit; a global lookup by id would be an IDOR.
risks.mitigation: Resolve strictly through the traversal, and throw IllegalArgumentException when Pet.getVisit returns null — the same refusal loadPetWithVisit already raises for an unknown owner or pet. Consistent with the existing route behaviour; the reader gets the error page.

risks.risk: Test trap on 'the stored visit still holds its previous date and description'. VisitControllerTests mocks OwnerRepository and returns one shared fixture, and binding mutates that fixture in memory on a refusal. Asserting the fixture's old values will fail even when the code is correct.
risks.mitigation: Observe the refusal as 'no write reached the repository' (no save call) plus the redisplayed form with the field error. Mockito interaction checking is tolerated here; the class already uses @MockitoBean.

risks.risk: An accidental flush on the refusal path if the handler ever becomes transactional. Today the refusal is safe only because spring.jpa.open-in-view is false and the handler is non-transactional, so the mutated graph is detached.
risks.mitigation: Leave both handlers non-transactional. Do not add @Transactional to VisitController.

risks.risk: The fixture's pet must carry a visit with an id. Owner.addPet ignores a pet that is not new, so the existing init() adds the pet before assigning its id.
risks.mitigation: Follow the same order for the visit: pet.addVisit(visit) then visit.setId(...), or set the id first since Pet.addVisit has no isNew guard.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit branches cleanly on the optional visitId, mirroring PetController.findPet's optional-path-variable shape (findPet, PetController.java:75).
Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer) exactly (identity lookup, isNew guard, Objects.equals, null on absence) — verified by direct comparison against Owner.java:117-127.
The non-future-date rule is extracted into one private helper (rejectVisitDateNotInFuture) shared by both POST handlers instead of duplicated, per the design-block's guidance.

processUpdateVisitForm relies on binding mutating the aggregate's own instance and calls owners.save with no add* call, avoiding the second-Visit-record risk the design-block flagged; the intent is documented in an inline comment at the call site.

VIEWS_VISIT_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM constant and initUpdateVisitForm/processUpdateVisitForm naming are consistent with the existing initNewVisitForm/processNewVisitForm pair and with PetController's VIEWS_PETS_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM convention.
checkFormat, checkstyleMain, and build/test/check all pass clean on the change set.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Owner-field binding on the correction POST is inherited, not introduced, but worth recording. processUpdateVisitForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner without @Valid and then persists it, so owner form parameters (firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone) posted to the correction URL bind onto the owner graph and are written by owners.save(owner), bypassing Owner's bean-validation constraints. processNewVisitForm has had exactly this shape since before the slice, and the identifier fields are protected by the @InitBinder disallow list, so the change is consistent with its neighbour and leaves the application no weaker than the baseline in system-design.md#security-context — not a finding under security-principles.md § Applying this section. A future slice that hardens it should harden both handlers together.

Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review. build.gradle, settings.gradle, and the Gradle wrapper are untouched by this change set, so the slice adds no dependency and clears no new-dependency check by construction. The OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (declared plugins: spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47), and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran. Spring Boot 4.1.0 governs the managed Jackson and Spring Framework versions; a human or CI should close the CVE check against the CycloneDX SBOM the build already produces.

The new endpoint is a state-changing POST with no CSRF token, like every other mutating route in the application. This is the recorded demonstration baseline (NG-1, system-design.md#security-context, threat-model row 1) and is explicitly not a reviewer finding under security-principles.md, but the surface has now widened by one route and the change-grader may want that in view.
approved_aspects: IDOR closed by construction: the corrected visit is reachable only by walking owner -> pet -> visit from a single owners.findById(ownerId). Pet.getVisit(Integer) searches only that pet's own visit set, so a visitId belonging to another pet or another owner resolves to null and loadPetWithVisit refuses with IllegalArgumentException. VisitControllerTests.theCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet exercises the foreign-visit path and asserts no save reached the repository. There is no VisitRepository and no global lookup by visit id anywhere in the diff.

Mass assignment / identifier tampering (security-principles.md Realization row 3, system-design.md#threat-model row 3): VisitController's @InitBinder is unnamed, so setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") applies to every model attribute bound by both the new GET and the new POST mapping, including the `visit` attribute that is now the stored entity instance. A submitted `id` or `*.id` parameter cannot repoint the correction at another row. No new binder was added that could omit the disallow list.

No second visit row: the correction path constructs no Visit and calls neither pet.addVisit nor owner.addVisit; binding mutates the instance already inside the aggregate and owners.save(owner) cascades. This closes the LinkedHashSet identity hazard the design-block flagged, and theCorrectedVisitShouldNotAddASecondVisitToThePet asserts the single-element outcome.

Fail-secure on refusal: rejectVisitDateNotInFuture plus @Valid run before any repository call, and the error branch returns the form without reaching owners.save. theRefusedCorrectionShouldLeaveTheStoredVisitUnchanged verifies no write reached the repository. spring.jpa.open-in-view=false and the absence of @Transactional keep the in-memory mutation detached, so a refused correction cannot flush.

Boundary re-resolution (security-principles.md Realization row 10): every request re-resolves owner, pet, and visit from the repository inside loadPetWithVisit. No identifier is trusted because an earlier request validated it.

Error-message hygiene: the new IllegalArgumentException text carries only the three identifiers the caller itself supplied in the path. Given the recorded defect that the error page renders the exception message (system-design.md#known-defects), this message leaks nothing the caller did not already know, and it matches the wording shape of the pre-existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found refusals.

XSS: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged and renders every request-derived value through th:text with Thymeleaf's default escaping on. No th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no template-preprocessing (__${...}__) construct appears in the diff or the reused template.

No new attack-surface classes: the diff contains no shell execution, no file or path handling, no deserialization configuration, no logging statements, no randomness, no network calls, and no hardcoded or newly committed credentials. Data access remains the single derived owners.findById plus save.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review (unchanged from round 1). build.gradle, settings.gradle, and the Gradle wrapper are absent from the round-2 change set, so the slice still adds no dependency. The OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured, and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran and this check must be read as 'not run', never clean. A human or CI should close the CVE check for Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its managed Jackson/Spring Framework versions against the CycloneDX SBOM the build already produces.

Owner-field binding on the correction POST is inherited, not introduced (carried forward from round 1). processUpdateVisitForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner without @Valid and then persists it, so owner form parameters posted to the correction URL bind onto the owner graph and are written by owners.save(owner), bypassing Owner's bean-validation constraints. processNewVisitForm has had exactly this shape since before the slice and the identifier fields are protected by the @InitBinder disallow list, so the slice leaves the application no weaker than the baseline in system-design.md#security-context. A future slice that hardens it should harden both handlers together.

The correction POST is a state-changing route with no CSRF token, like every other mutating route in the application. This is the recorded demonstration baseline (NG-1, system-design.md#security-context, threat-model row 1) and is explicitly not a reviewer finding under security-principles.md, but the mutating surface has widened by one route and the change-grader may want that in view.

The refusal path throws IllegalArgumentException carrying the ownerId, petId, and visitId from the request back into the message, which surfaces as a 500 page. It mirrors the pre-existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found messages in the same method, discloses only ids the caller already supplied, and REQ-SYS-002's error-detail defect is already recorded in docs/system-design.md#known-defects. Worth folding into that defect's eventual fix rather than treated separately.
approved_aspects: Round-2 delta contains no production change. scripts/changeset.sh --name-only shows src/main/java/.../Pet.java and VisitController.java identical to the tree approved in round 1 (build-pass line 22: 'No production code changed'); the delta is the new PetTests.java, one added VisitControllerTests case, and the ADR/PRD/system-design edits closing the doc-reviewer finding. No new attack surface entered the change set.

IDOR remains closed by construction and is now more thoroughly proven. The corrected visit is reachable only by walking owner -> pet -> visit from a single owners.findById(ownerId); Pet.getVisit(Integer) searches only that pet's own visit set, so a visitId belonging to another pet or to no pet resolves to null and loadPetWithVisit refuses with IllegalArgumentException. Both halves of PRD edge case 3 are now exercised: theCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet and the newly added theCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitDoesNotExist, each asserting then(owners).should(never()).save(any(Owner.class)). There is no VisitRepository and no global lookup by visit id anywhere in the change set.

Mass assignment / identifier tampering (security-principles.md Realization row 3, system-design.md#threat-model row 3): VisitController's @InitBinder is unnamed, so setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") applies to every model attribute bound by both the new GET and the new POST mapping. Re-verified unchanged at VisitController.java:53-56.

The new PetTests unit test hardens rather than weakens the identity lookup: theLookupShouldSkipAVisitThatHasNeverBeenSaved pins the !visit.isNew() guard, which is what stops an in-flight unsaved visit (id null) from answering a lookup for a null id. That guard is the reason a null or absent visitId cannot be steered onto an unrelated in-memory instance.
No secrets in the change set. grep for password/secret/token/apikey/credential over the four changed Java files returns nothing; the new test constants are ids, dates, and descriptions only.

Detection-pattern sweep over the owner package is clean: no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec(, no system /tmp usage, no @JsonTypeInfo or enableDefaultTyping, no shell or SQL string interpolation. The change set introduces no file I/O, no XML parsing, no deserialization, and no outbound network call.

Output escaping unchanged: templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is absent from the change set and continues to render the visit description through th:text (contextual escaping), not th:utext, and uses no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) on request-supplied text. The correction path reuses that same template, so the corrected description is escaped on the way out.

Documentation delta is security-neutral: the ADR/PRD/system-design edits move the NG-5 narrowing onto the Status line and References, add the REQ-VISITEDIT-001 narrative and the detached-graph persistence paragraph. No claim in system-design.md#security-context or #threat-model was altered, weakened, or contradicted.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: One module and one package: two production files (83 lines) add Pet.getVisit plus a GET and a POST on VisitController, reusing the existing booking template and touching no schema, dependency, or configuration. The reach worth naming is that the mutating HTTP surface grows by one route that persists the whole owner aggregate, on an application with no authentication and no CSRF token anywhere - the recorded demonstration baseline, not something this change introduces.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk. The correction path returns the stored Visit out of the loaded owner graph so binding updates it in place and nothing is added to the pet; the isNew guard in Pet.getVisit stops a null visitId matching an unsaved in-flight visit; and the extracted rejectVisitDateNotInFuture is equivalent to the logic it replaces. The one counterintuitive consequence - a visit whose date has already passed cannot have only its description corrected, because the future-date rule refuses it - is deliberate and written into the PRD as edge case 4 and an open question rather than hidden.

test_adequacy.note: The new tests assert real outcomes and would fail against plausible breakages: singleElement pins that no second visit is added, the two refusal tests pin the owner-to-pet-to-visit walk, and PetTests covers all three getVisit branches. The gap is the slice's central persistence claim - that mutating a detached visit and calling owners.save cascades an UPDATE - which is verified only against a Mockito mock of OwnerRepository and asserted in prose in the new system-design paragraph. The JPA-layer suite ClinicServiceTests proves the analogous claim for booking (shouldAddNewVisitForPet) and gained no update counterpart, so a cascade that silently did nothing would leave the whole suite green.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved with empty findings, but the security reviewer attached four recommendations to a round-2 approval, one of them addressed to this grader by name. Two reach the human: the supply-chain check must be read as not run rather than clean (no NVD access, no dependency-check plugin configured), and the correction POST binds and persists Owner fields without @Valid - inherited from processNewVisitForm, now on a second route.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the requirement's stated surface exactly, including the deliberate omission of any page linking to the correction form. Zero build retries and zero consultations. The single design revision was a documentation-placement fix - moving the NG-5 narrowing out of the 2026-08-08 ADR decision body onto its Status line - not a scope wander, and the narrowing itself is an owner decision carrying its own ADR.

rationale: Correct and well tested at the controller level, but confirm the correction actually writes before merging: the detached-graph cascade is proven only against a mock, with no JPA-level update test beside the existing booking one. Note also the security reviewer's not-run supply-chain check.
